title: Minimax Value Estimation for Spillover Policies under Partial Interference and Hölder Smoothness
banked_reason: The note proves exact fixed-shift critical-window risk and honest-length limits, but the promised uniform joint frontier remains open and the delivered paper is incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The proposal promises a sharp uniform joint K,m,|q-p| frontier with attaining procedures and design thresholds, but this node expressly leaves that frontier unresolved; the delivered finite modulus and on-policy/fixed-shift slices do not supply the promised all-regime object.
The advertised joint frontier, including shrinking policy shifts and explicit consistency and design thresholds, remains open in oeq:joint-frontier; global one-cutoff optimality also remains open.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a finite Hölder-modulus characterization and proved exact fixed-shift critical-window point-risk and honest-length constants, including the ancillary-randomized interval construction. It did not uniformly evaluate the modulus when |q-p| shrinks, because that requires new multiscale lower bounds and either global cutoff optimality or a multi-cell upper construction. The sound endpoint results therefore bank at incremental novelty.
tldr: For independent partial-interference clusters with one binary focal outcome each, the finite H\"older modulus characterizes minimax value risk and honest interval length up to constants. At a fixed policy shift in the binomial critical window, the point-risk limit is \(L^2G^2m^{-\beta}\), and the shortest uniformly honest expected length has exact leading term \(2(1-\alpha)LGm^{-\beta/2}\). The joint frontier when the policy shift shrinks, and global one-cutoff optimality, remain open.
gap: Generic linear-functional moduli and partial-interference policy estimands are known. Zamolodtchikov (2026) gives continuous-design Hölder covariate-shift prediction rates, including a pure-transfer upper result. The inspected work does not evaluate the scalar-value modulus for a noisy, growing discrete binomial lattice with jointly changing source-target separation; search coverage is bounded.
fill: Establish the full joint risk and honest-length diagram, including polynomial and logarithmic factors, match it with a legal Bernoulli lower submodel and an attaining transport estimator and interval, and use the result to select a single saturation for multiple targets.
